chunks: And from him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ibn Ribat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the eggs of the ostrich. He said: 'It is treated in the same way as sheep [i.e., its meat is halal], just as the eggs of the ostrich are treated in the case of camels.' And as for the report which we mentioned earlier from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'That in the eggs of the ostrich there is the freshness (or first quality) of sheep.'

key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: Sheep (used here as a category for halal land animals)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating ostrich eggs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of expiation (kaffarah) by establishing an analogical ruling (qiyas) for ostrich eggs, equating their legal status to that of sheep meat rather than camel meat. This distinction is crucial for determining the specific sacrificial animal required when a pilgrim commits a minor violation, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise categorization of game animals based on their biological and legal attributes.
